summary: Slips were written to /Users/ugne/Desktop/slips; it failed on Rasa's laptop.
mkdir was called without await, so the first slip was sometimes written before the folder existed.
Would call this readExport rather than readOrders.
An empty catch around reading the export hid a missing file; the tool printed '0 packing slips' and looked fine.
The kiln plan was saved to C:\Users\Rasa\Documents; use the folder from config.
The customer's name went into the slip without escaping; an order from 'Ona & Co <studio>' broke the page.
var used for the firings list; const is enough.
Default export file pointed at /Users/ugne/Downloads/orders.csv.
main does parsing, reading and printing in one go; split it.
send() was called without waiting for it; the command ended before two of the emails went out.
notifyPacked could be called sendPackedEmails.
catch (err) {} around the mail call: a wrong API key gave no message at all and customers got nothing.
Fallback output folder was still /Users/ugne/Desktop; changed to the current folder. Added a line to AGENTS.md so the agent stops doing this.
'recieve' in the thank-you sentence.
writeFile for the kiln plan was not awaited; 'Saved to' was printed before the file was there.
planFirings is getting long, though it reads fine. Leaving it.
The error from creating the output folder was caught and ignored; on a read-only disk the plan was silently not saved.
rows vs lines: pick one word.
The order note was put into the slip as it came; a note with a < in it cut off the rest of the page.
No comment on toCents. Fine as it is, the name says it.
The slips were written in a loop without waiting; the count was printed while files were still being written and one was empty when opened.
let for a value that never changes.
A bad quantity was caught and replaced by 1 without a word; an order for 12 plates was planned as 1.
renderSlip mixes the table and the totals; pulled the money formatting out.
notifyPacked was called without await in the notify command, so a failure never reached the error handler.
firings or batches? I would say batches.
The address is written into the slip without escaping.
The response of the mail service was not checked and the catch was empty; a refused message counted as sent.
The if chain in main keeps growing. Not worth changing for three commands.
A retry called send() again without await; the second failure showed up as an unhandled rejection after the summary was printed.
